points: The Nov. 3 Q3 print will show whether the adjusted 3% year-over-year revenue decline and the 37% EPS drop seen in Q2 ($0.26 vs. $0.41 a year earlier) are stabilizing or still deteriorating, which is central to the short case.

Q3 guidance and any Q4/FY2 commentary will reveal whether the staffing rebound has enough momentum to justify the consensus FY2 EPS jump of 55%, from $1.27 to $1.97; reports suggest the market is treating that guide as the key test.

Talent solutions posted its third consecutive quarter of sequential adjusted growth and permanent placement grew 2.5% year-over-year in Q2, but the print will show whether those narrow positives can offset broader global enterprise revenue weakness.
Q2 net income fell to $26 million from $41 million a year earlier on lower revenue, so the Q3 results will reveal whether operating leverage is still negative as revenue remains under pressure.

The stock trades at about 35x forward earnings and a 1.7x premium to the theme median, so the print will show whether that valuation can survive the 4.2% consensus FY1 EPS cut and the 90-day revenue estimate drift of -3.7%.
With 30-day analyst revisions running 5 downgrades versus 3 upgrades, the print will likely set the direction of estimate momentum into Q4 and any initial 2027 guidance.
UPWK reports a week later on Nov. 10, but RHI’s own Q3 results and FY2 outlook are the immediate catalyst for the trade.
watch: Q3 revenue versus Q2’s $1.336 billion and the year-ago $1.370 billion — another decline supports the short.
Q3 EPS versus Q2’s $0.26 and the year-ago $0.41 — continued compression supports the short.
FY2 EPS guidance / Q4 implied run-rate needed to reach the $1.97 consensus — a lack of upward revision supports the short.
Permanent placement adjusted year-over-year growth and talent solutions sequential growth — any slowdown supports the short.
